```{r}
#| label: setup
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(targets)

work <- tar_read(work_scale)
flow <- tar_read(dataset_flow)
measured <- tar_read(measured)
pooled <- tar_read(screen_pooled)
units <- tar_read(described_units)
week <- tar_read(week_pooled)
relations <- tar_read(relations_pooled)
outcomes <- tar_read(outcomes_pooled)
by_year <- tar_read(screen_by_year)
by_year_share <- tar_read(screen_by_year_share)
datasets <- tar_read(dataset_table)
manifest <- tar_read(data_manifest)
settings <- tar_read(settings)
exposures <- tar_read(exposure_registry)
schema <- tar_read(dataschema)

fmt <- function(x) format(round(x), big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)
num <- function(x, digits = 2) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = digits)
pct <- function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", 100 * x)
range_of <- function(mid, low, high, f = num) paste0(f(mid), " (", f(low), " to ", f(high), ")")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 10))
stage_order <- settings$school_stage_labels

# Plain labels: an exposure's name with its day, and a variable's schema label.
exposure_names <- c(
  total = "Total screen time", watch = "Watching", game = "Gaming",
  socmedia = "Social media", educational = "Educational use", comp = "Computer",
  tablet = "Tablet", phone = "Phone", educontent_watch = "Educational programmes",
  internet = "Internet", leisure = "Leisure screen use", messaging = "Messaging",
  videochat = "Video chat", creating = "Creating content", email = "Email",
  shopping = "Shopping", work = "Paid work on a screen",
  comp_nongaming = "Computer, other than gaming", game_comp = "Gaming on a computer",
  game_console = "Gaming on a console", game_handheldconsole = "Gaming on a handheld console",
  game_active = "Active video games", game_phone = "Gaming on a phone",
  game_tablet = "Gaming on a tablet", violent_watch = "Violent programmes",
  violent_game = "Violent games", violent_watch_index = "Violent programmes (index)",
  violent_game_index = "Violent games (index)"
)
label_exposure <- function(x) coalesce(exposure_names[x], x)
label_measure <- function(variable) {
  row <- match(variable, exposures$variable_name)
  day <- c(usual = "", weekday = ", weekday", weekend = ", weekend day")[exposures$day[row]]
  ifelse(variable == "total_screen", "Total screen time", paste0(label_exposure(exposures$exposure[row]), coalesce(day, "")))
}
label_variable <- function(variable) coalesce(schema$label[match(variable, schema$variable_name)], variable)
```

A working draft of the descriptive half of the report to the funder, built before any model is run.
Screen use and outcomes are described separately here: nothing relates one to the other.
Every figure is computed within each study's own waves and countries first and then pooled so that each dataset counts once; a figure needs `r settings$min_datasets` or more datasets.
Distributions, weekday and weekend means and prevalences use survey weights where the study released them; the correlations between screen measures do not.
No dataset is named.
Data: `r nrow(manifest)` datasets, overall hash `r unique(manifest$overall_hash)`.

## The scale of the work

```{r}
#| label: totals
work$totals |>
  transmute(` ` = item, Count = fmt(count)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

Each of the `r fmt(nrow(schema))` shared variables was considered for each dataset, and the decision recorded with its reason; a few datasets record extra decisions where they measure screen use twice.

```{r}
#| label: flow
flow |>
  mutate(across(c(datasets, participants, rows), \(x) ifelse(is.na(x), "", fmt(x)))) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("Stage", "Datasets", "Participants", "Observations"), align = "lrrr", caption = "Datasets from specification to analysis. Datasets identified or requested but never specified are not recorded in the repository, so the earlier stages are not shown.")
```

```{r}
#| label: files
work$files |>
  filter(role == "data") |>
  transmute(Format = reader, Datasets = datasets, Files = fmt(files)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "Raw data files read, by format.")
```

```{r}
#| label: mapping
status_labels <- c(
  compatible = "Compatible: converts to the shared variable without loss",
  partial = "Partial: part of the construct, or a simplification",
  proximate = "Proximate: a close but not equivalent set of categories",
  inferred = "Inferred: from the study's design or documentation",
  incompatible = "Incompatible: related information exists but cannot be used",
  unavailable = "Unavailable: the study did not collect it",
  in_progress = "Not yet decided"
)
work$mapping |>
  mutate(order = match(status, names(status_labels))) |>
  arrange(order) |>
  transmute(`Mapping decision` = coalesce(status_labels[status], status), `Decisions` = fmt(rows), Datasets = datasets) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: schema
work$schema |>
  arrange(desc(rows)) |>
  transmute(Domain = domain, `Shared variables` = rows) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

## Who is in the data

```{r}
#| label: who
tibble::tibble(
  ` ` = c(
    "Datasets",
    "Countries and territories, as the studies record them",
    "Collection years",
    "Waves and countries analysed separately (units)",
    "Datasets by design",
    "Datasets with survey weights"
  ),
  Value = c(
    nrow(datasets),
    n_distinct(na.omit(units$country)),
    paste(round(min(units$year, na.rm = TRUE)), "to", round(max(units$year, na.rm = TRUE))),
    fmt(nrow(units)),
    paste(paste(table(datasets$design), names(table(datasets$design))), collapse = "; "),
    paste0(sum(datasets$weighted), " of ", nrow(datasets))
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The count of countries follows the studies' own labels, so the nations of the United Kingdom, and some territories, are counted separately.

```{r}
#| label: fig-year-age
#| fig-height: 4
#| fig-cap: "Observations by collection year and the unit's median age. Numbers are datasets; cells with fewer than 30 observations are left out."
units |>
  filter(!is.na(year), !is.na(age_median)) |>
  mutate(year = 5 * floor(year / 5), age = 2 * floor(age_median / 2)) |>
  summarise(rows = sum(rows), datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), .by = c(year, age)) |>
  filter(rows >= settings$min_unit_rows) |>
  ggplot(aes(year, age, fill = rows)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets), size = 2.5, colour = "white") +
  scale_fill_viridis_c(trans = "log10", labels = scales::comma, name = "Observations") +
  labs(x = "Collection year (five-year bands)", y = "Median age of the unit (two-year bands)")
```

```{r}
#| label: countries
units |>
  mutate(country = coalesce(country, "(not recorded)")) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), rows = sum(rows), .by = country) |>
  filter(rows >= settings$min_unit_rows) |>
  arrange(desc(datasets), desc(rows)) |>
  transmute(Country = country, Datasets = datasets, Observations = fmt(rows)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr", caption = "Countries and territories, by how many datasets include them.")
```

## What was measured

### Screen use

```{r}
#| label: measured-exposures
measured$exposures |>
  filter(day == "usual", context == "any") |>
  mutate(kind = c(activity = "Activity", device = "Device", subset = "A subset of an activity", aggregate = "Aggregate")[axis]) |>
  transmute(Measure = label_exposure(exposure), Kind = kind, Datasets = datasets, `Dataset-waves` = dataset_waves, Values = fmt(scores)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "Usual-day screen measures, by how many datasets hold them.")
```

```{r}
#| label: how-measured
units |>
  filter(!is.na(measure_type)) |>
  summarise(datasets = n_distinct(dataset_id), units = n(), rows = sum(rows), .by = c(measure_type, responder)) |>
  arrange(desc(rows)) |>
  transmute(`Response format` = measure_type, `Who reported` = coalesce(responder, "(not recorded)"), Datasets = datasets, Units = units, Observations = fmt(rows)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "How screen use was asked: response bands (categorical) against open entry (continuous), and who answered.")
```

### Outcomes

Scores add up the values of every shared variable under an outcome, so a child with a parent report and a self report is counted twice: the column shows the volume of data, not a number of children.

```{r}
#| label: measured-outcomes
measured$outcomes |>
  transmute(
    Family = prereg_family,
    `Specific outcome` = label,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Dataset-waves` = dataset_waves,
    Scores = fmt(scores),
    `Shared variables` = schema_rows,
    Informants = informants,
    `Score types` = score_types
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrll")
```

## How much children use screens

Medians and shares lead, because response bands with an open top make means understate heavy use.
Each cell gives the median dataset's value, with the range the middle half of datasets span.
A dataset's own value is the average of the medians of its waves and countries, so for a rarely used measure it can fall between the response options.
"Reporting none" counts answers of exactly zero, which depends on whether a questionnaire offered "none".

```{r}
#| label: distributions
usual <- exposures$variable_name[exposures$day %in% "usual" & exposures$exposure != "total"]
pooled |>
  filter(grouping == "all", variable_name %in% c(usual, "total_screen")) |>
  arrange(variable_name != "total_screen", desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
    `How built` = built,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Median hours a day` = range_of(median_mid, median_low, median_high),
    `Upper quartile` = range_of(p75_mid, p75_low, p75_high),
    `Reporting none` = range_of(share_zero_mid, share_zero_low, share_zero_high, pct),
    `2 hours or more` = range_of(share_2plus_mid, share_2plus_low, share_2plus_high, pct),
    `4 hours or more` = range_of(share_4plus_mid, share_4plus_low, share_4plus_high, pct)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrrrrr")
```

Total screen time is shown by how it was built, and its rows are not comparable with each other: a sum of more content classes is larger because more was asked, and a sum of three classes is not always the same three.

```{r}
#| label: fig-by-stage
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Median hours a day by school stage: the median dataset (point) and the middle half of datasets (line). Numbers are datasets."
pooled |>
  filter(grouping == "school_stage", variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_comp", "st_phone")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = stage_order), measure = label_measure(variable_name)) |>
  ggplot(aes(group, median_mid)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = median_low, ymax = median_high), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets, y = median_high), vjust = -0.6, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Median hours a day") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: by-sex-ses
pooled |>
  filter(grouping %in% c("sex", "ses_household"), group %in% c("Female", "Male", "Low", "Medium", "High"), variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational")) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = c("Female", "Male", "Low", "Medium", "High"))) |>
  arrange(variable_name, group) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
    Group = group,
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Median hours a day` = range_of(median_mid, median_low, median_high),
    `2 hours or more` = range_of(share_2plus_mid, share_2plus_low, share_2plus_high, pct)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr", caption = "By sex, and by household socioeconomic position relative to the study's own sample.")
```

## Weekdays and weekends

Compared on the same children, where a study asked both.
Means are shown here, because the comparison is within a study's own response format.

```{r}
#| label: week
week |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_exposure(exposure),
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Mean hours, weekday` = range_of(mean_weekday_mid, mean_weekday_low, mean_weekday_high),
    `Mean hours, weekend day` = range_of(mean_weekend_mid, mean_weekend_low, mean_weekend_high),
    `Share using more on a weekend day` = range_of(share_more_on_weekend_mid, share_more_on_weekend_low, share_more_on_weekend_high, pct)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrr")
```

## Change over time

Each unit's mean hours against the year its data were collected, in one model that splits the trend in two.

The **between-study** part compares studies run in different periods.
They also differ in country, age and how they asked, so it is adjusted for the units' ages and, where they vary, the response format and who reported; it remains the weaker evidence, because which studies exist in each period is not random.

The **within-study** part follows like units of one study through its years: the same country, school stage, respondent and response format, and no recorded change to the question.
Where a study redesigned its question, the years before and after are treated as separate series, so a redesign is not read as change over time.
It is the firmer evidence, and it usually rests on few studies; where the estimate has fewer than 4 degrees of freedom it reads "too few studies to say".

A trend needs `r settings$year_min_datasets` or more datasets spanning `r settings$year_min_span` or more years.
Total screen time is left out, because it is built differently from dataset to dataset.

```{r}
#| label: by-year-table
year_table <- function(trend, what, f = num) {
  fitted <- filter(trend$trends, status == "fitted")
  if (nrow(fitted) == 0) return(knitr::kable(tibble::tibble(Note = "No measure has enough datasets and years.")))
  part <- function(est, low, high, status) case_when(
    is.na(est) ~ "",
    status == "too few studies to say" ~ "too few studies to say",
    TRUE ~ range_of(est, low, high, f)
  )
  fitted |>
    arrange(desc(k_datasets)) |>
    transmute(
      Measure = label_measure(variable_name),
      Datasets = k_datasets,
      Units = k_units,
      Years = paste(round(first_year), "to", round(last_year)),
      Between = part(between_per_decade, between_ci_low, between_ci_high, between_status),
      Within = part(within_per_decade, within_ci_low, within_ci_high, within_status),
      `Studies with a series over years` = k_within,
      `Adjusted for` = adjusted_for
    ) |>
    knitr::kable(align = "lrrlrrrl", col.names = c("Measure", "Datasets", "Units", "Years in the data", paste("Between studies:", what, "per decade"), paste("Within studies:", what, "per decade"), "Studies with a series over years", "Between part adjusted for"))
}
year_table(by_year, "change in mean hours a day")
```

```{r}
#| label: by-year-share
year_table(by_year_share, "change in the share at 2 hours or more, in percentage points", \(x) num(100 * x, 1))
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-by-period
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Mean hours a day by five-year period: the median dataset (point) and the middle half of datasets (line), each dataset counted once per period. Numbers are datasets; periods with fewer than three are not shown. Different studies make up each period, so this is the unadjusted picture."
by_year$periods |>
  filter(variable_name %in% c("st_watch", "st_game", "st_socmedia", "st_educational", "st_comp", "st_phone")) |>
  mutate(measure = label_measure(variable_name)) |>
  ggplot(aes(period, mid)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = low, ymax = high), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets, y = high), vjust = -0.6, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(measure), scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Collection years (five-year periods)", y = "Mean hours a day")
```

## How the kinds of screen use relate

Rank correlations between two screen measures among the same children, within each unit.
These are unweighted.

```{r}
#| label: relations
relations |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(
    Measure = label_measure(variable_a),
    With = label_measure(variable_b),
    Datasets = datasets,
    `Rank correlation` = range_of(spearman_mid, spearman_low, spearman_high),
    `Share doing both` = range_of(share_both_mid, share_both_low, share_both_high, pct)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrrr")
```

## Binary outcomes

Prevalence within each unit, pooled so that each dataset counts once.
Standardised scores are not shown, because they carry no meaning on their own.

```{r}
#| label: outcomes
outcomes |>
  filter(grouping == "all") |>
  arrange(desc(datasets)) |>
  transmute(Outcome = label_variable(variable_name), Datasets = datasets, Prevalence = range_of(prevalence_mid, prevalence_low, prevalence_high, pct)) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-outcomes-stage
#| fig-height: 6
#| fig-cap: "Prevalence by school stage for the binary outcomes with most datasets: the median dataset (point) and the middle half (line). Numbers are datasets."
by_stage <- filter(outcomes, grouping == "school_stage")
top <- by_stage |> summarise(k = max(datasets), .by = variable_name) |> slice_max(k, n = 6, with_ties = FALSE)
by_stage |>
  filter(variable_name %in% top$variable_name) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = stage_order), outcome = label_variable(variable_name)) |>
  ggplot(aes(group, prevalence_mid)) +
  geom_linerange(aes(ymin = prevalence_low, ymax = prevalence_high), colour = "grey50") +
  geom_point() +
  geom_text(aes(label = datasets, y = prevalence_high), vjust = -0.6, size = 2.5) +
  facet_wrap(vars(outcome), scales = "free_y", labeller = label_wrap_gen(30)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Prevalence") +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1))
```

## The datasets

One row per dataset, numbered and not named.

```{r}
#| label: dataset-table
datasets |>
  transmute(
    Dataset = dataset_id,
    Design = design,
    Countries = countries,
    Years = ifelse(round(first_year) == round(last_year), as.character(round(first_year)), paste(round(first_year), "to", round(last_year))),
    `Median age of its units` = ifelse(round(youngest) == round(oldest), as.character(round(youngest)), paste(round(youngest), "to", round(oldest))),
    Waves = waves,
    Observations = fmt(participants_rows),
    `Shared variables supplied` = variables_supplied,
    Weights = ifelse(weighted, "yes", "")
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "llrllrrrl")
```
